evidence: add-address.usecase.ts: ErrorFactory.UseCaseError(`User with id ${userId} not found`, null, HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND) after OwnedResourceAccessPolicy.canMutateResource fails, and 'User not found' with HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND when userResult.value is null
delete-address.usecase.ts: ErrorFactory.UseCaseError(`User with id ${userId} not found`) with no status for the denial; ErrorFactory.UseCaseError('User not found') with no status for the missing user
set-default-address.usecase.ts and update-address.usecase.ts: ErrorFactory.UseCaseError(`User with id ${userId} not found`) with no HttpStatus in both branches
add-address.usecase.ts / update-address.usecase.ts take AddAddressCommand / UpdateAddressCommand from '../../../commands/'
delete-address.usecase.ts declares `export interface DeleteAddressInput`; set-default-address.usecase.ts declares `export interface SetDefaultAddressInput` instead of command classes
delete-address and set-default-address check `userResult.isFailure`; add and update use `isFailure(userResult)`
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The four use cases share one concern: changing addresses on the User aggregate. Each delegates the business logic to the aggregate (addAddress, deleteAddress, setDefaultAddress, updateAddress) and saves with optimistic versioning, so cohesion is fine.

The problem is duplication. Each file has its own copy of the authorize → load-for-update → 'not found' → save sequence, and with it the rule that a denied mutation looks like 'User not found'. Those copies have already drifted apart:
- AddAddressUseCase passes HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND to ErrorFactory.UseCaseError for both the denial and the missing-user case.
- The other three call ErrorFactory.UseCaseError(message) with no status, so the same condition probably yields a different HTTP status.
- The 'not found' messages also differ: 'User not found' versus `User with id ${userId} not found`.

The module also uses its input abstractions inconsistently:
- AddAddressUseCase and UpdateAddressUseCase take Command objects from application/commands.
- DeleteAddressUseCase and SetDefaultAddressUseCase declare their own inline input interfaces (DeleteAddressInput, SetDefaultAddressInput) and skip the commands folder.

Smaller inconsistencies: some files check failure with isFailure(...) and others read .isFailure directly, and some import shared-kernel through relative paths while others use 'src/' paths.

Together these show the rule living in several places instead of one, and the module's own command abstraction applied in only half of the use cases.

violations.message: Has its own copy of the rule that a denied mutation is reported as 'not found'. Unlike its sibling use cases, it adds HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, so the same condition gets a different status depending on the operation.
Declares an inline DeleteAddressInput instead of using the module's command abstraction. Also repeats the access-denied/not-found mapping, with no status and a different message ('User not found').
Declares an inline SetDefaultAddressInput instead of a command from application/commands. Also repeats the authorize/load/not-found sequence without the NOT_FOUND status that AddAddressUseCase uses.
Repeats the access-denied/not-found mapping without HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, which disagrees with AddAddressUseCase.
